item.title: CLI: Command Line Interface
item.description: A CLI is an AI tool that works in the terminal, inside a folder on your computer.

item.title: Queryable Knowledge Base
item.description: A student looking for Peter Brinson's Office Hours, the game design guide itself? Click here.Here to learn what a queryable knowledge base is, and build one? Read on.

item.title: Peter Brinson — Teaching
item.description: Course materials and talks. Personal site: peterbrinson.com.

item.title: Persistent Workspace
item.description: A persistent workspace is a folder on your computer that both you and an AI return to, session after session.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: Obsidian is a free text editor for markdown files. It shows your folder and file structure in a sidebar, the way VS Code does for a codebase.

item.title: In-Context Learning
item.description: In-context learning means the AI learns from what you place in front of it, live, in the moment: the files it’s holding in memory for this session.

item.title: Context Engineering
item.description: Context engineering is the craft of arranging your files so an AI finds what matters without being told every time: which files it reads, in what order, and how much it can hold at once.

item.title: Artifact
item.description: An artifact is a finished piece of work an AI hands you, something you can keep, read, review, and pass along.
